messages.author: 17f8070912132195
messages.subject: Error: .onLoad failed in loadNamespace() for 'utils'
parts:
Dear INLA group,

I defined a latent model using rgeneric. The model ran successfully on my local computer, but I received an error message when running it on an HPC cluster. Could this be related to some system settings?  I appreciate your guidance on this issue.

Here is the error message:
"During startup - There were 13 warnings (use warnings() to see them)
Error: .onLoad failed in loadNamespace() for 'utils', details:
  call: system(paste(which, shQuote(names[i])), intern = TRUE, ignore.stderr = TRUE)
  error: 4 arguments passed to .Internal(system) which requires 3

 *** ERROR ***: source R-file [/home/rbi/YFT_pp_nq/nq_0-noPS-Tweedie_ar1_Aniso/inla.model/results.files/inla_rgeneric_wrapper_nWWkpR] failed.

 *** inla.core.safe:  The inla program failed, but will rerun in case better initial values may help. try=1/1
During startup - There were 13 warnings (use warnings() to see them)
Error: .onLoad failed in loadNamespace() for 'utils', details:
  call: system(paste(which, shQuote(names[i])), intern = TRUE, ignore.stderr = TRUE)
  error: 4 arguments passed to .Internal(system) which requires 3

 *** ERROR ***: source R-file [/home/rbi/YFT_pp_nq/nq_0-noPS-Tweedie_ar1_Aniso/inla.model-1/results.files/inla_rgeneric_wrapper_ZB1zXZ] failed.
Error in inla.core.safe(formula = formula, family = family, contrasts = contrasts,  :
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.
The inla program failed and the maximum number of tries has been reached."

Thanks,
Ruby

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error: .onLoad failed in loadNamespace() for 'utils'
parts:
On Wed, 2024-10-30 at 14:21 -0700, Ruby Ji wrote:
> call: system(paste(which, shQuote(names[i])), intern = TRUE, ignore.stderr =
> TRUE)
>   error: 4 arguments passed to .Internal(system) which requires 3

this msg indicate a version mismatch in R, since what its compiled with is not
what its getting.

I guess it loads an older version of libR.so which cause the error. 

I guess you have done

inla.binary.install()

for your HPC OS _after_ doing

inla.upgrade(testing=TRUE)

then restart R, and do

inla.setOption(verbose=TRUE,debug=TRUE)
demo(rgeneric)

and send me the output


--
Håvard Rue
he...@r-inla.org
